one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly used underparameterized single-parameter distribution families (one-peak, Zipf, exponential) that cannot simultaneously satisfy two independent KL divergence constraints, then treated out-of-tolerance results (~0.3-0.7 error) as 'very close' and saved noncompliant outputs, concluding the task may be 'mathematically impossible' rather than adopting a correct multi-level structured approach.
t_err_evidence: At step 6 the agent switches to a one-parameter alpha model (single dominant mass with uniform tail), explicitly designing a family with only one degree of freedom to satisfy two independent KL constraints (KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10). This is a structural design error: one free parameter cannot satisfy two independent equations in general.
t_commit_evidence: At step 6 the underparameterized family (single-peak scalar model) is adopted and never replaced with a correctly parameterized multi-level structure throughout the remaining 27 steps. All subsequent scripts (two-level, power-law, Zipf, exponential, piecewise mixtures) share the same fundamental flaw of insufficient degrees of freedom, locking in failure from step 6 onward.
t_surface_evidence: Step 7 execution of find_distribution_optimized.py shows Forward KL: 11.917365 and Backward KL: 10.014969, both outside the required ±0.001 tolerance around 10.0, providing the first concrete observable failure signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the mathematical insight that satisfying two independent KL constraints simultaneously (KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10) requires at least two free parameters (e.g., a two-level distribution with both the probability ratio and the count of high-mass elements as variables, solved via a 2D search or nonlinear system). Instead, it repeatedly constructs single-parameter families, grid-searches single dimensions, and applies underparameterized heuristics, never recognizing that the parametric families chosen are structurally incapable of hitting two independent targets.
forewarning_evidence: Step 2: The LLM step analysis (pre-execution assessment) flags 'non_scalable_optimization_choice' noting BFGS on 150,000 parameters is infeasible and that a low-parameterized family should be used. Step 3: ModuleNotFoundError on numpy shows environment issues. Step 5: OptimizeWarning about unknown solver option. These are all warning signals before the underparameterized approach fully commits at step 6.
